# Error codes

A failed command returns one typed envelope: `code`, `number`, `message`, `vt_us` (the virtual time), `retryable`, an optional `hint`, and `detail`, `serial_tail` and `backtrace` where they apply. With `--output json` it is that JSON object; as text it is the code, the message and the hint. Quote the code and follow the hint.

| Code | Number | Group | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `E_USAGE` | 1 | `core` | The arguments are wrong: an unknown argument, a value outside its type or its enumerated set, or a required one missing. Nothing ran; fix the call and repeat it. |
| `E_STATE` | 2 | `core` | The call is well formed but the instance cannot serve it in the state it is in, such as no instance at all, one already stopped, or one whose boot has not reached the point the command needs. |
| `E_STALE_REF` | 3 | `core` | A reference taken from an earlier revision no longer names anything, such as a `ui` `eN` object ref after the tree moved on. Take a fresh revision and look it up again. |
| `E_TIMEOUT` | 4 | `core` | The condition the command was told to wait for did not hold within the virtual-time budget it was given. Retryable: repeat it with a longer budget. |
| `E_WALL_BUDGET` | 5 | `core` | The call used more of the host's own wall-clock budget than it is allowed, whatever virtual time it reached. Retryable, and it changes no result. |
| `E_LEASE` | 6 | `core` | Someone else holds the clock lease this command needs, or the caller does not hold it. The message names the holder. |
| `E_GUEST_PANIC` | 7 | `core` | The guest firmware panicked. The envelope carries the reason, the task, the decoded frames, `mcause` and `mtval`, and the tail of the console. |
| `E_DEADLOCK` | 8 | `core` | Every guest task is waiting and nothing left in the machine can wake one, so virtual time cannot advance. The envelope carries the task table and the lock owners. |
| `E_STUCK` | 9 | `core` | The guest is spinning on a value nothing in this build will ever change. The envelope names the block, register, program counter and symbol it is waiting on. |
| `E_TRIPWIRE` | 10 | `core` | The guest reached something the emulator refuses to run rather than fake, such as a disabled radio feature or an access outside an allowlist. The message names the cause. |
| `E_UNMODELED` | 11 | `core` | The guest touched hardware this build does not model. `inspect --json '{"what": ["fidelity"]}'` lists what was unmodeled in the run. |
| `E_HLE_BINDING` | 12 | `core` | High-level emulation could not bind to the image: the symbols it needs are absent, or they do not match the profile's expectation. Raised when the binding is made, not later. |
| `E_ASSET_MISSING` | 13 | `core` | A file the run needs is not there: an unknown corpus id, a corpus entry whose file is gone, an unreadable path, or no bundled ROM for the eFuse's chip revision. |
| `E_ASSET_HASH` | 14 | `core` | The bytes are there but are not the pinned ones: a corpus file that differs from the SHA-256 `corpus.toml` records, or a ROM override outside `assets/rom/pins.toml`. |
| `E_SNAPSHOT` | 15 | `core` | A snapshot could not be saved, restored, exported or imported, most often because it belongs to a different run identity (ROM, image, eFuse or config). |
| `E_SECRET_REFUSED` | 16 | `core` | The call would have returned bytes the secret policy does not release, such as a read wholly inside masked memory or an export of secrets without an explicit human step. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | 17 | `core` | The emulator itself failed, or the part of it this command needs has not landed in this build. It says nothing about the firmware under test. |
| `E_HLE` | 18 | `core` | A bound high-level-emulation handler failed the call it intercepted, or a nested guest call did not have the stack headroom its guard requires. Binding itself was fine. |
| `E_HOST_UNSUPPORTED` | 19 | `core` | The command, or one option of it, does not exist on this host. The message names this host and the one that supports it; the host columns of the command pages say so ahead of time. |
| `E_DAEMON` | 20 | `core` | The shared daemon could not be reached or started: no port answered with the token, the connection dropped mid-call, or the runtime directory is unusable. Retryable. |
| `E_PLAN_REFUSED` | 5000 | `device` | The flash planner refused the plan before writing anything to a real device, and reset the device back to its app. The message says which check refused it. |
| `E_DEVICE_BUSY` | 5001 | `device` | The real device the plan names is already held by another operation. |
| `E_CARDID_CHANGED` | 5002 | `device` | The device's cardid partition is not the one the plan was made against. It carries instructions for a person, never an automated repair: this tool never writes cardid. |
